---
title: Explore panel quality
jupyter: python3
---

Checking missing values and outliers in the member-day panel:

- `data/interim/panel.parquet` (`align`): every universe member × every trading day of its quarter; `close`, `ret`, market columns `rf`/`mkt_ret`/`vix`, raw features, NaN kept
- `data/processed/panel.parquet` (`clean`): features ranked per date to [-1, 1], NaN → 0; prices/returns/market columns untouched

(see `src/factor_weaver/data/build/panel.py`)

```{python}
import os
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path

while not (Path.cwd() / "config" / "data.yaml").exists() and Path.cwd().parent != Path.cwd():
    os.chdir("..")
print(Path.cwd())

raw = pd.read_parquet("data/interim/panel.parquet")
proc = pd.read_parquet("data/processed/panel.parquet")
KEYS = ["date", "ric", "permid"]
COLS = [c for c in raw.columns if c not in KEYS]
MARKET = ["rf", "mkt_ret", "vix"]
FEATURES = [c for c in COLS if c not in ["close", "ret", *MARKET]]
```

## Interim

### Shape

```{python}
members = raw.groupby("date").size()
pd.Series({
    "rows": len(raw),
    "days": raw["date"].nunique(),
    "first": raw["date"].min().date(),
    "last": raw["date"].max().date(),
    "members/day min": members.min(),
    "members/day max": members.max(),
    "duplicate (date, ric)": raw.duplicated(["date", "ric"]).sum(),
})
```

### NaN % per column

```{python}
raw[COLS].isna().mean().mul(100).round(2).sort_values(ascending=False)
```

### NaN % per column by year

```{python}
raw[COLS].isna().groupby(raw["date"].dt.year).mean().mul(100).round(1)
```

### Members with missing prices

```{python}
miss = raw.loc[raw["close"].isna()]
miss.groupby("ric")["date"].agg(["count", "min", "max"]).sort_values("count", ascending=False)
```

### Dates with missing market columns

```{python}
raw.loc[raw[MARKET].isna().any(axis=1), ["date", *MARKET]].drop_duplicates()
```

### Distribution

```{python}
raw[COLS].describe(percentiles=[0.001, 0.01, 0.5, 0.99, 0.999]).T
```

### Outliers per column (|robust z| > 10, median/MAD)

```{python}
x = raw[COLS].drop(columns="close")  # price levels are not comparable across stocks
z = (x - x.median()) / (1.4826 * (x - x.median()).abs().median())
z.abs().gt(10).sum().sort_values(ascending=False)
```

### Largest absolute returns

```{python}
raw.loc[raw["ret"].abs().nlargest(20).index, ["date", "ric", "close", "ret", "mkt_ret"]]
```

### Largest robust z per feature

```{python}
pd.DataFrame(
    {f: raw.loc[z[f].abs().idxmax(), ["date", "ric", f]].set_axis(["date", "ric", "value"]) for f in FEATURES}
).T.assign(z=z[FEATURES].abs().max().round(1))
```

## Processed

### Same rows and untouched columns

```{python}
same = ["close", "ret", *MARKET]
pd.Series({
    "same keys": raw[KEYS].equals(proc[KEYS]),
    "same close/ret/market": raw[same].equals(proc[same]),
    "NaN in features": int(proc[FEATURES].isna().sum().sum()),
})
```

### Feature range and NaN-filled share

```{python}
pd.DataFrame({
    "min": proc[FEATURES].min(),
    "max": proc[FEATURES].max(),
    "mean": proc[FEATURES].mean().round(3),
    "% was NaN (→ 0)": raw[FEATURES].isna().mean().mul(100).round(1),
    "% zero": proc[FEATURES].eq(0).mean().mul(100).round(1),
})
```
